question.explanation:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

\begin{align*} -4e^z + 7 &= 5 \\[5pt] -4e^z &= -2 \\[5pt] e^z &= \dfrac{1}{2} \end{align*}

Then, we find the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $z\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} e^z &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^z\right) &= \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \\[3pt] z &= -\ln\left(2\right) \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $z = -\ln\left(2\right).$

example.title: Finding Solutions to Exponential Equations when Rearrangement is Required

question.text: Find the solution to the equation $e^{8x} = \sqrt{5}$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
First, we take $\ln$ of both sides of the equation:

\begin{align*} e^{8x} &= \sqrt{5} \\[3pt] \ln \left(e^{8x}\right) &= \ln\left(\sqrt{5}\right) \\[3pt] 8x &= \ln\left(5^{1/2}\right) \end{align*}

Then, we apply the power rule to the right-hand side and solve for $x$:

\begin{align*} 8x &= \dfrac 1 2\ln(5) \\[5pt] x &= \dfrac {1}{16} \ln(5) \end{align*}

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

\[ x \approx 0.101 \] rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Finding Approximate Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.explanation:
First, we take $\ln$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} e^{2x+3} &= 7 \\[5pt] \ln \left(e^{2x+3}\right) &= \ln(7) \\[5pt] 2x+3 &= \ln(7) \\[5pt] 2x &= \ln(7)-3 \\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{\ln(7)-3}{2} \end{align*}

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives \[ x \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-0.527} \] rounded to $3$ decimal places.
